item.title: Digital Transformation and Service
item.content:encoded:
Christian Bartelheimer, University of Göttingen

Daniel Beverungen, Paderborn University

Sara Hofmann, University of Agder

Lysanne Lessard, University of Ottawa

Digital transformation continues to reshape how organizations create, deliver, and capture value. At the same time, service has become a crucial lens for understanding contemporary information systems (IS) phenomena. Value is co-created across organizational boundaries, enacted through digital technologies, and embedded in networks, platforms, and ecosystems. The Topical Collection on Digital Transformation & Service at Electronic Markets seeks to advance theoretically grounded and relevant IS research at the intersection of digital transformation and service.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digital transformation and service in information systems
  • Design and application of IT artifacts to foster value co-creation
  • Smart service systems and ecosystems at multiple levels (communities, organizations, inter-organizational arrangements, platforms, data spaces, and society)
  • Customer relations, value propositions, and service exchange enabled by digital technologies
  • Role of digital technologies in real-world service scenarios
  • Inter-organizational contexts such as service networks, digital platforms, data spaces, and business ecosystems
  • Digital transformation in established organizations, start-ups, public-sector organizations, and communities
  • IT artifacts using or expanding large language models and other large-scale artificial intelligence technologies
  • Generative AI and digital responsibility in service contexts
